It illustrates her struggle between her longing for a life tied to the river and the sacred call of the Begijnhof. Further, the chapter shifts to Wivina, who cherishes her wealth and heritage but is eventually called to a life of poverty and devotion by St. Francis, setting the stage for her internal conflict between material wealth and spiritual fulfillment. As the stories unfold, the rich tapestry of human emotion and spiritual exploration begins to take shape, inviting readers into the enchanting world of the beguines.
